documents: Lu et al. 2022, Hydrological Processes 36:e14751, published paper (PDF, 13 pages)

entry.evidence: there has been no study conducted that has quantified the sediment load in the Upper Mekong catchment within China

sequences.source_document: Lu et al. 2022, Hydrological Processes, published version

steps.action: States three aims: quantify sediment yield and load from the Mingyong glacial catchment, analyse their temporal variability, and discuss drivers and implications for the Upper Mekong.
steps.quote: this study aims to: (1) quantify the sediment yield and sediment load from the Mingyong glacial catchment

steps.action: Selects the Mingyong Glacier catchment for its position at the southeastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau and its low latitude, and sites a single sampling station 3.1 km below the terminus for access reasons.
steps.quote: This glacial catchment was selected due to its position at the southeastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau

steps.action: Designs a sampling schedule weighted to high flows: five to six samples per month in June to August, at least two in October to March, following monthly precipitation and temperature.
steps.quote: the frequency of collection was higher during periods of high flow to capture the high transport rates

steps.action: Measures discharge by the float method and cross-sections surveyed at low flow, and suspended sediment concentration by filtering triplicate 500 ml samples, over 158 sampling events with a gap from September 2014 to August 2015; attempted bedload measurements could not be completed.
steps.quote: In total there were 158 sampling events from August 2013 to July 2017

steps.action: Fits a power-law SSC-Q sediment rating curve to the full record by Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least squares and obtains a poor fit (R2 = 0.40) with large scatter above 25 m3/s.
steps.quote: We used a power function to fit the sediment rating curve

steps.action: Because of the poor overall fit, refits the rating curves separately for each hydrological year (R2 0.42 to 0.62).
steps.quote: Due to the poor fit, the rating curve was fitted by hydrological years

steps.action: Because large scatter remained at high discharge, splits each year into rising and falling stages (Table 1); fits improve except the 2013 falling stage (R2 = 0.11).
steps.quote: the SSC-Q relationship improved when the data was categorized into falling and rising stages

steps.action: Plots monthly-mean SSC-Q hysteresis loops and finds a clockwise loop in each of the three hydrological years and in calendar year 2016.
steps.quote: Hysteresis loops for the three hydrological years were represented by clockwise hysteresis

steps.action: Interprets the clockwise hysteresis as proximal sediment supply on the rising limb and depletion of sediment availability by the end of the ablation season, drawing on cited hysteresis literature.
steps.quote: The patterns across the three hydrological years suggest the sediment availability is depleted by the end of the ablation season

steps.action: Interpolates daily discharge linearly, applies the stage-specific rating curves to estimate daily, monthly and annual loads and yields, and reports the seasonal concentration of load and a monthly load-discharge correlation (R2 = 0.82).
steps.quote: However, annual sediment load variability was large, ranging from 44 kilotons (kt) in 2013 to 91 kt in 2015

steps.action: Poses two rival controls of sediment flux, air temperature (melt) and precipitation, and describes the melt and monsoon-rainfall mechanisms for each from the literature.
steps.quote: Dominant control of sediment fluxes: temperature or precipitation?

steps.action: Compares the interannual sediment yields with annual precipitation, extreme-precipitation days and mean temperature at Deqin station (Figures 6 and 7).
steps.quote: These interannual variations seem to be mainly driven by the differences in annual precipitation rather than the mean annual temperature

steps.action: Sets aside glacial melt dynamics as the main driver of interannual variability because temperature varied little over the study period, while noting that extreme melting events were absent.
steps.quote: the temperature variations detected within our study period pales in comparison to precipitation variations

steps.action: Compiles published sediment yields from glacierized Tibetan Plateau basins (Table 2) and plots yield against basin area and glacier coverage with the Mingyong values (Figure 8).
steps.quote: The sediment yield for the Mingyong Glacier catchment is relatively high compared with sediment yields from other glacierized basins on the Tibetan Plateau

steps.action: Explains the high yield by the small, heavily glacierized basin, the short distance from the glacier snout, steep slopes and relatively high precipitation, and raises threshold effects as a possible cause of the variability, left for future study.
steps.quote: The high sediment yield of the Mingyong glacial catchment can be explained by its small but heavily glacierized (68%) basin area

steps.action: Retains annual sediment yields for three hydrological years as baseline measurements for the Mekong headwaters.
steps.quote: Based on the in-situ observations over three hydrological years, the sediment yields are estimated to be

tree.answer: Suspended sediment flux from a proglacial Upper Mekong catchment, unquantified
Discharge and SSC measured directly; loads and yields inferred via rating curves
Quantify sediment yield and its seasonal and interannual variability
Temperature (melt) versus precipitation as the control of interannual variability
Conditions found: natural seasonal and annual hydroclimate at one station

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Three hydrological years and seasonal cycles repeat; rating curves and hysteresis fitted per year
No variation or replication of the estimates reported
Yields estimated; precipitation argued to dominate interannual variability

end.claim: From in-situ measurements over three hydrological years, the Mingyong catchment's suspended sediment yield was about 1104, 2281-2283 and 1833 t/km2/year in 2013, 2015 and 2016, with 65-78% of the annual load in June-August.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the 158 in-situ discharge and SSC sampling events at a site where no gauge existed, no rating curves or yields could have been estimated.

gates.evidence: Sampling was scheduled by the flow regime, not directed by a hypothesis (p. 3-4). The yield estimates faced no independent check: no uncertainty is propagated to loads and no held-out or turbidity data are used. The precipitation-over-temperature argument rests on a three-year visual comparison (pp. 8-9). Nothing was fixed in advance beyond the sampling schedule.

imports.item: Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least-squares fitting in Origin 2021b
0.45 μm Whatman nylon membrane filters and Nalgene vacuum filtration unit

novelty_claims.quote: to our best knowledge, there has been no study conducted that has quantified the sediment load in the Upper Mekong catchment within China
This study has provided a benchmark dataset
the data fills the knowledge gap in sediment data for the headwaters of the Mekong River

limits: No V check is performed. Yields carry no stated uncertainty: rating-curve 95% intervals are shown in Figure 4 but not propagated, so the estimate_with_resolution status is generous. The claim that precipitation controls interannual variability rests on three years and is best_explanation at most. The temperature rival is set aside qualitatively, with the caveat that extreme melting events were absent. The 2015 yield is given as 2281 (abstract, p. 7, Table 2) and as 2283 (pp. 8, 11). Annual water discharge differs between the text (0.50, 0.46, 0.53 km3) and Table 2 (0.5, 0.5, 0.46). The abstract's range ends in 2016 while the 2016 value is lower than 2015. Bedload was attempted but not quantified, so total load is underestimated (inference). A one-year gap (Sept 2014 to Aug 2015) and linear interpolation of discharge between sampling dates are not tested for sensitivity. Climate data come from Deqin station, 13 km away. The paper does not state whether the stage split was chosen before or after the poor fits were seen; the text implies after.

disagreements.target: temperature-sensitive glacier dynamics as driver of interannual sediment yield (Costa et al., 2018; Stott & Mount, 2007)
disagreements.support: Over three years at Mingyong, yields tracked annual precipitation and extreme-rain days while temperature varied little; the authors restrict the claim to the absence of extreme melt events.
disagreements.quote: we argue that the interannual variations in the sediment yield in the Mingyong Glacier catchment are largely determined by precipitation rather than glacial melt dynamics

alternatives_considered.chosen: Separate power-law rating curves for rising and falling stages of each hydrological year
alternatives_considered.alternatives: A single rating curve for the whole record; curves by hydrological year only
alternatives_considered.reason: Poor fit of the single curve (R2 = 0.40) and hysteretic and seasonal effects

alternatives_considered.chosen: Cross-section surveyed in February, September, November and April
alternatives_considered.reason: Danger when conducting measurements during the high-flow summer discharge

alternatives_considered.chosen: Hand sampling, float method and hand depth measurement
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Automated hydrology equipment such as data loggers or turbidity meters (recommended for future studies)
alternatives_considered.reason: Hand methods could introduce random errors; automated equipment could increase sampling frequency and accuracy

alternatives_considered.chosen: Precipitation as the dominant control of interannual variability
alternatives_considered.reason: Temperature variations within the study period were small compared with precipitation variations
